title: Katz index de Independence dans Activities de Daily Living (ADL)
short_title: Indice de Katz d’indépendance dans les activités de la vie quotidienne (ADL)
abbreviations: Katz Index of Independence in Activities of Daily Living (ADL)
formula:
The Katz Index of Independence inADLis determined by the number of the following six activities the patient can perform independently:

| Activities | Independence 1 | Dependence 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bathing (E.g., sponge, shower, or tub) | Bathes self completely or requires assistance with bathing only a single part (e.g., back, disabled extremity) | Requires assistance with bathing more than one part of the body, getting in or out of the tub/shower, or does not bathe self |
| Dressing | Retrieves clothes from closets and drawers; puts on clothes, outer garments, and braces; manages fasteners (tying shoes is excluded) | Does not dress self or remains partially undressed |
| Toileting | Gets to the toilet; gets on and off the toilet; arranges clothes; cleanses self after elimination (may manage own bedpan at night only and may or may not use mechanical supports) | Uses a bedpan or commode or requires assistance getting to or using the toilet |
| Transferring | Moves in and out of bed and chair independently (may or may not use mechanical supports) | Requires assistance moving in or out of bed and/or chair; does not perform one or more transfers |
| Continence | Maintains complete control of urination and defecation | Has partial or total incontinence of urination or defecation; requires enemas, catheters, or regulated use of urinals and/or bedpans |
| Feeding | Gets food from plate (or equivalent) into mouth; (precutting meat and food preparation, such as buttering bread, are excluded from evaluation) | Requires assistance with feeding, does not eat at all, or receives parenteral feeding |

1. Without supervision, direction, or active personal assistance.
2. With supervision, direction, active personal assistance, or total care; patients who refuse to perform a function are considered dependent in that function, even if physically able.

how_to_use.why:
- Standardizes the assessment of a patient’s ability to perform basic activities of daily living (ADLs) to improve team communication (e.g., clinician, PT/OT).
- Results correlate with a patient’s risk of adverse outcomes (e.g., falls, hospitalization, mortality).
- Easy to repeat and document, allowing tracking of changes over time.
- Can support prevention of disability and help maintain rehabilitation gains.
- Integrated into some prognostic assessment tools (e.g., [RHMP-30](nabda:calc.rotterdam-hip-fracture-mortality-prediction-30-days-rhmp-30) ) as a functional status component.
how_to_use.when:
- À utiliser pour évaluer le statut fonctionnel de base chez les personnes âgées et les personnes ayant des limitations fonctionnelles (p. ex., maladie chronique, atteinte neurologique).
- À appliquer pour quantifier un nouveau déclin fonctionnel après une maladie aiguë ou une lésion et pour surveiller la progression de l’incapacité liée à des affections chroniques.
- À répéter pour suivre la trajectoire fonctionnelle et la réponse aux interventions au fil du temps.
- Peut être utilisé dans différents contextes de soins (p. ex., ambulatoire, hospitalier, post-aigu) et comme outil administré par un clinicien ou par le patient/le proche aidant.
how_to_use.pearls:
- Initialement développé chez des personnes âgées présentant des fractures de la hanche, puis appliqué au fil des années à d’autres populations de patients, notamment les personnes atteintes de maladie neurologique, de maladie cardiovasculaire, de néoplasie, de maladie pulmonaire chronique et d’autres affections chroniques.
- Souffre d’un effet plancher, ce qui le rend relativement insensible aux variations à de faibles niveaux d’incapacité fonctionnelle.
- N’évalue pas les fonctions de niveau supérieur, telles que les activités instrumentales de la vie quotidienne (IADLs) et les activités avancées de la vie quotidienne (AADLs).

next_steps.advice:
- Use results to assess a patient’s ability to perform ADLs; a full functional assessment should also include IADLs and, when relevant, AADLs.
- Results can inform discharge planning and care needs based on identified deficits, such as:

 - Physical and/or occupational therapy programs.
 - Fall-prevention measures.
 - Home safety evaluations.
 - Long-term care planning.
 - Caregiver support services.
- Trend results over time to follow progress with rehabilitative and supportive interventions.

more_info:
Interpretation

| Katz Index | Grade |
| --- | --- |
| Independent in all six functions | A |
| Independent in all but one of the functions | B |
| Independent in all but bathing and one additional function | C |
| Independent in all but bathing, dressing, and one additional function | D |
| Independent in all but bathing, dressing, toileting, and one additional function | E |
| Independent in all but bathing, dressing, toileting, transferring, and one additional function | F |
| Dependent in all six functions | G |
| Dependent in at least two functions, but not classifiable as C, D, E, or F | Other |
medium_description: Assesses basic functional status pour help quantify disability et care needs.
